discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 270549
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
149 AM EDT Tue Oct 27 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Warm and dry conditions persist through tomorrow with highs 
  generally in the low 70s and lows in the low 50s.

- Light rain is possible on Thursday. The best chances (50-80%) will 
  be near Lake Michigan.

- Better chances for widespread rain arrive on Sunday but
  forecast confidence for this period is low.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 146 AM EDT Tue Oct 27 2026

Yesterday's frontal boundary has washed out completely across our 
area but we do have a brief return to easterly flow this morning. 
Luckily numerous high clouds, a steady gradient wind and an overall 
warmer/drier boundary layer are keeping fog in check. Flow veers to 
a more S/SE direction by this afternoon and highs should recover to 
around 70F outside of our far NE. Warm/moist air advection then 
steadily increases tonight through Thu ahead of the next cold front 
headed for our area. Expect more mid 70s on Wed and some upper 70s 
possible by Thu dependent on exact frontal timing. As previously 
mentioned, Thursday's frontal passage will feature a much better 
prefrontal LLJ and theta-e surge, enough to at least partially 
offset the incredibly dry and stable airmass that has been in place 
for so long. Mid/upper level support is still not great this far 
south with far better CVA and upper jet support over Lake Superior 
and points north. Still, enough moisture advection and low level 
convergence to generate some very light rain showers with the best 
chances near Lake Michigan Thursday afternoon. Latest guidance even 
suggests a few sprinkles surviving into our SE Thu evening. No 
impacts anticipated though. Removed the brief/small NBM thunder 
mention given near total lack of instability on forecast soundings. 

A return to less extreme warmth Fri and Sat with highs around 70F. A 
very high level of spread still exists among all sources of 
deterministic and ensemble guidance for the weekend into next week. 
This uncertainty centers around an unusually southward displaced 
Pacific jet streak/shortwave emanating from the data-sparse regions 
off the Mexican coast that will eventually lift northeast into our 
region. Models struggling with this and another upper low that 
develops off the northwest U.S. coast. Very low confidence regarding 
forecast details Sat-Tue. Still think Halloween will be mostly dry 
for trick-or-treat activities but NBM maintains some low chance 
PoP's and can't entirely rule it out. Much better rain chances seem 
to arrive Sunday with remarkable uncertainty regarding a potential 
second system around Tuesday of next week.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z WEDNESDAY/...
Issued at 146 AM EDT Tue Oct 27 2026

A mid level ridge axis will shift across the eastern Great Lakes
this morning allowing continuation of some mid level warm
advection cloudiness. Fog potential continues to look much lower
in comparison to previous several mornings, and a VFR forecast
has been maintained with the 06Z TAFs. Surface high pressure 
across southern Ontario will spread across southeast 
Ontario/southern Quebec this afternoon as larger scale sfc 
pressure falls develop across the Upper Midwest downstream of an
upper level short wave trough. This evolution will allow for 
initial easterly winds to veer southeast today, but speeds 
should be 10 knots or less through the day. A southern stream 
short wave across the southern Plains will reach the Ohio Valley
tonight, but any weakly pooled moisture to the north of stalled
baroclinic zone will retreat to the north. This will keep dry 
conditions in place through this period.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...AGD

spc.text:
SPC AC 270528

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1228 AM CDT Tue Oct 27 2026

   Valid 271200Z - 281200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are not expected today.

   ...Synopsis...
   A large-scale trough will be maintained across the West on Tuesday
   with ridging remaining across the East. Several embedded mid-level
   shortwave troughs will be present within this western trough,
   including across the central Plains.

   High pressure across much of the CONUS will limit thunderstorm
   activity. The only exception will be across the southern High Plains
   where some lee troughing and moisture return will be present. A few
   thunderstorms may develop within a region of relatively greater
   instability (1000 to 1500 J/kg MLCAPE) across southeast New Mexico
   and Far West Texas. Shear will be relatively weak, but there could
   be enough flow for some marginal supercell structures. Hail could be
   possible with the strongest storms, but it should remain below
   severe limits. Outside of this area any storm activity should remain
   weak and unorganized.

   ..Bentley/Thornton.. 10/27/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 270520

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1220 AM CDT Tue Oct 27 2026

   Valid 281200Z - 291200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorm potential appears low on Wednesday.

   ...Mid-MO to Upper MS Valley...

   A midlevel trough will move from the High Plains to the Upper MS
   Valley on Wednesday. This will bring enhanced mid/upper
   southwesterly flow across the Mid-MO to Upper MS Valley atop
   modestly increasing boundary layer moisture. Vertically veering wind
   profiles and effective shear values greater than 35 kt typically
   could support supercell thunderstorms. However, surface-based
   thunderstorm develop appears quite conditional. Surface dewpoints in
   the 50s to near 60 F will be possible ahead of a surface boundary
   from southern MN into western IA and far eastern NE. Cool
   temperatures atop the modest boundary layer moisture will support
   MLCAPE values around 1000 J/kg. Near neutral height tendencies are
   expected, and forecast soundings indicate poor low-level lapse rates
   and possible inhibition in layers between the surface and 750 mb.
   Furthermore, 00z HRRR/RRFS and HREF/REFS do not show a robust signal
   for sustained convection within the more favorable warm sector.
   While elevated storms could pose a risk for small hail, the overall
   risk appears limited in the absence of surface-based storms,
   precluding severe probabilities at this time. Depending on trends,
   probabilities could be included in subsequent outlooks. 

   ...Far SW TX vicinity...

   Isolated thunderstorms may develop near higher terrain within a
   modest upslope flow and low-level warm advection regime late
   Wednesday afternoon/early evening. Surface dewpoints in the
   mid/upper 50s will aid in modest destabilization as temperatures
   warm into the upper 70s/low 80s F. Deep-layer flow is expected to be
   weak, but vertically veering profiles will support around 20-25 kt
   effective shear magnitudes. A couple of storm could briefly become
   strong and produce gusty winds given steepened low-level lapse rates
   or small hail. Overall, severe potential appears too limited to
   include probabilities.

   ..Leitman.. 10/27/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 270629

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0129 AM CDT Tue Oct 27 2026

   Valid 291200Z - 301200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are not expected on Thursday.

   ...Synopsis...

   Scattered showers and thunderstorms are expected across portions of
   NM/TX and into the Plains on Thursday as a midlevel shortwave trough
   moves across the southern Rockies into the southern Plains.
   Deep-layer southwesterly flow is expected to remain modest, and any
   stronger flow aloft will remain confined to the northern tier of the
   U.S. South/southeasterly low-level flow will maintain 50s to low 60s
   dewpoints across the southern Plains toward the Lower MO Valley
   vicinity. This will support a band of modest destabilization from
   eastern NM into KS on the nose of stronger low-level warm advection.
   However, the area of any appreciable destabilization is expected to
   be displaced from the modest large-scale ascent provided by the
   ejecting southern stream shortwave. Overall, severe thunderstorm
   potential appears low.

   ..Leitman.. 10/27/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
